name: Luanda
subtitle: Luanda, capital of Angola: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,194,747 people live in the municipality of Luanda (counted 2014).
Luanda was founded by Paulo Dias de Novais, whose fleet reached the island of Luanda in February 1575; he created a permanent settlement named S. Paulo de Luanda on the mainland.
Novais placed the settlement on the mainland rather than the island because of its good defensive conditions and, above all, its sheltered port.

parts.text: Luanda was founded by Paulo Dias de Novais, whose fleet reached the island of Luanda in February 1575; he created a permanent settlement named S. Paulo de Luanda on the mainland.
Novais placed the settlement on the mainland rather than the island because of its good defensive conditions and, above all, its sheltered port.
The expedition was well received by the Ngola, who authorised the founding of Luanda.
Luanda became the centre of Portuguese presence and influence in the region for centuries, except for the period 1641-1648 under Dutch control.
In the 17th century Luanda became the main slave-export port of the Atlantic world, sending from Angola much of the labour demanded by Brazil and the Spanish Indies.
At the 2014 census the municipality and city of Luanda had 2,194,747 residents, the most populous in the province, followed by Viana (1,605,291).
The 2014 census counted 6,945,386 residents in the province of Luanda.
INE projected Luanda as the most populous province in 2022, with 9,079,811 inhabitants (27.4% of the national total).
In 2021 the Port of Luanda handled nearly 7.8 million tonnes, 73.3% of all cargo moved through Angolan ports.
In 2021 the Port of Luanda accounted for 90.7% of container traffic in Angolan ports.
The median age of Luanda's population is 21.1 years, according to the 2014 census results reported by Lusa.
